title: status-live-probe: status and system-status must probe live runtime/storage, not return hardcoded defaults
description: Feature P1-11. Master §33.3 Lifecycle Command Surface requires status and system-status to be operational tools, not stubs. Today vb_cli/src/commands/status.rs:29 build_status constructs Shard::new(ShardConfig::default()) and reads the defaults, returning hardcoded '0' counters. The test at status.rs:176-188 confirms this. vb_cli/src/commands/system_status.rs:7 has a const NO_BACKEND_REASON and emits connected: false, health: degraded, ... always. The status command is the operator's first stop when diagnosing issues; hardcoded output is worse than no output. This bead: (1) adds Runtime::storage_health() -> StorageHealth returning Healthy | Degraded { reason } | Unreachable; (2) changes cmd_status to try opening an IPC client to --server; on success send IpcCommand::Health; on failure fall back to transient-shard view; (3) same for cmd_system_status; (4) adds --server <path> flag to status.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL report live runtime and storage health from a real probe, not from hardcoded defaults
THE SYSTEM SHALL fall back to a transient-shard view with a `fallback_reason` field when the live server is unreachable, never silently returning defaults

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user runs `vb status --server <socket>` and the server is reachable
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL connect, send IpcCommand::Health, and return the live StorageHealth and counters

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user runs `vb status` with no --server
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL open a transient shard, return a snapshot view, and include fallback_reason: 'no --server specified; transient shard view'

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user runs `vb status --server <socket>` and the server is unreachable
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 3 with `ServerUnreachable` and include the socket path and last error

unwanted.condition: IF the Fjall journal is locked by another process (single-server model per master §68.2)
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT silently return StorageHealth::Healthy; it must return Unreachable with reason 'journal locked by another process'
unwanted.because: Operators must know the server is not actually serving traffic

unwanted.condition: IF the runtime is in a degraded state (e.g., shard queue > 80% full)
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT return Healthy; it must return Degraded with a specific reason
unwanted.because: Operators need to know to scale up or back off

preconditions: Either a --server <socket> is provided and the IPC server is running, OR no --server is provided and the transient-shard fallback is acceptable
postconditions: StatusReport.connected is true if the server responded, false otherwise
StatusReport.health is one of: Healthy | Degraded { reason } | Unreachable { reason }
StatusReport.counters reflect the live runtime (not zero) when connected
invariants: No status call returns hardcoded '0' counters when the server is reachable
fallback_reason is always present when connected: false, never silently omitted

happy: status_with_running_server_returns_live_counters: start ipc-serve, run `vb status --server <socket>`; counters are non-zero for a workload that has been processed
status_without_server_returns_transient_view_with_fallback_reason: `vb status` (no --server) returns a snapshot with fallback_reason: 'no --server specified'
system_status_probes_fjall_health: `vb system-status --db /tmp/db` opens the Fjall journal, runs a probe (read of /ready keyspace), returns Healthy or Unreachable
error: status_with_locked_journal_returns_unreachable: two processes try to open the same Fjall path; the second gets Unreachable with reason 'journal locked'
edge: status_health_proptest: proptest over 100 random shard states, assert health classification is correct

files: crates/vb_storage/src/fjall.rs (FjallJournal health probe; check if /ready keyspace exists)
patterns: Pattern: existing IPC client construction in other commands (e.g., cmd_inspect opens an IPC client to --server)
Pattern: StorageHealth enum: Healthy | Degraded { reason: String } | Unreachable { reason: String }
questions: Is IpcCommand::Health already implemented? (Spec: yes, per master §21.16.)
Does FjallJournal expose a /ready keyspace for the probe? (Spec: not yet; this bead adds it.)

security_failures.failure: An attacker masks a degraded runtime by spoofing the --server socket, returning Healthy when the real server is Degraded
security_failures.prevention: Use a Unix domain socket with filesystem permissions; reject connections from other UIDs

usability_failures.failure: Operator runs `vb status` expecting live data, gets hardcoded zeros, and concludes the system is fine when it's actually broken
usability_failures.prevention: Always include fallback_reason when not connected; never return zeros silently

data_integrity_failures.failure: The transient-shard view reads a fresh empty shard, returning '0 active runs' when there are actually 100 active runs in the persistent journal
data_integrity_failures.prevention: When falling back to transient, emit a clear warning in stderr: 'WARNING: transient view; live server unreachable'

integration_failures.failure: StatusReport schema changes and breaks an external monitoring tool
integration_failures.prevention: Schema is versioned; new fields are additive only

phase_0: Read crates/vb_ipc/src/commands.rs to confirm IpcCommand::Health exists
Read crates/vb_storage/src/fjall.rs to find the Fjall journal handle
phase_1: Write proptest test_status_health_proptest (100 random shard states)
phase_2: In vb_runtime/src/runtime/mod.rs: add `pub fn storage_health(&self) -> StorageHealth` that probes Fjall (try opening the /ready keyspace) and returns the enum
In vb_storage/src/fjall.rs: add a /ready keyspace that is written on open and read by the probe

In vb_cli/src/commands/status.rs: replace build_status with a new build_live_status that opens an IPC client to --server; on success, send IpcCommand::Health and populate from the response; on failure, populate from a transient shard with fallback_reason
In vb_cli/src/commands/system_status.rs: replace the const NO_BACKEND_REASON with the same live probe pattern
In args: add --server <path> flag to status (default: no server; transient view)
phase_3: Add StorageHealth enum to vb_runtime::runtime (Healthy | Degraded | Unreachable)
phase_4: Run `moon run :test -p vb_cli -p vb_runtime -p vb_storage` and verify all new tests pass
Manual: `vb ipc-serve --db /tmp/db & vb submit foo.yaml --db /tmp/db && vb status --server <socket>` should show non-zero counters

similar_implementations: cmd_inspect opens an IPC client to --server; pattern to copy

key_sections_to_understand: The test at line 176-188 that confirms the bug

apis_that_exist: Shard::new(ShardConfig::default()) in vb_runtime::shard (used for transient view)
apis_that_do_not_exist: Runtime::storage_health() does not exist; this bead adds it
no_placeholder_values: Do NOT use 0 as a 'no data' placeholder; use Option<u64> or a typed Unreachable
